title: devkit.json
description: A project's config: how it uses the kit, and the facts about itself the kit needs. It sits at the project root and is project-owned. The code reviewer reads it from the project's checkout on every run, and the generator turns it into the project's kit-owned files. Both validate against this file through one small interpreter (plugin/devkit-config.mjs), which understands only the keywords used here: a new keyword fails its tests until it learns it.

$schema.description: Where this schema lives, for editors. Ignored by the kit.

modules.description: The kit's modules the project uses. Only "process" exists so far, so it must be listed; "web" and "canvas" are accepted and not yet acted on.

kit.description: The kit commit the project's kit-owned files were last generated from, as a full or abbreviated SHA. For the record only: whether a project is behind the kit is decided by regenerating its files, not by this value.

sweep.description: Retired, and ignored by a code reviewer that runs on the owner's machine, which sweeps every project in one nightly run. Still accepted so that a project whose sweep is still dispatched by GitHub Actions keeps validating.

hour.description: Retired with `sweep`. The hour of the day, in UTC, at which a project still on GitHub Actions has its nightly sweep dispatched.

reviewer.description: How the code reviewer sets the project up and tests it. Commands run with `sh -c` from the project root of a fresh checkout, without the code reviewer's own credentials in their environment.

setup.description: Run once after each checkout, before the tests and before any agent works in the tree, to install dependencies and the like. Must be safe to run again on a tree it has already run in.

tests.description: The project's test suites. Each is run on every audit round, and its result is put in front of the auditors; the fixer is told to run them.

name.description: A short name for the suite, shown in the reports.

command.description: The shell command that runs the suite. A non-zero exit is a failing suite.

env.description: Environment variables for the project's setup, test and nightly check commands, and only for them. The same role as the action's `repo-env` input, which wins on a name both set: the input is where a secret can come from, and this file is committed. A name the code reviewer keeps for itself, `DATABASE_URL` say, may be set here; it reaches the project's commands without ever entering the code reviewer's own environment.

databases.description: The environment variables that each need a database of their own. Before setup, the code reviewer creates one empty Postgres database per name on the machine it runs on, of that machine's Postgres version, and puts each one's address in its variable for the project's setup, test and nightly check commands, over a value `env` gives the same name. The databases are dropped after the run. A machine that cannot create them fails the run, saying what is missing.

services.description: Retired, and ignored by the code reviewer: on the owner's machine the tests get their databases from `databases`. Still accepted for a project whose tests still run in GitHub Actions: services the tests need, in the shape of a GitHub Actions job's `services:` map, keyed by the service's id. The generator writes them onto the jobs of the project's sweep workflow that run the tests (`sweep` and `review-now`). Their connection details reach the tests through `env`.

image.description: The Docker image to run, `postgres:16` say.

env.description: Environment variables for the service container.

ports.description: Ports to publish, as GitHub Actions takes them: `5432:5432` or a bare container port.

volumes.description: Volumes to mount, as GitHub Actions takes them.

options.description: Extra `docker create` options, a health check say.

credentials.description: Registry credentials for a private image.

harnessNotes.description: Path, relative to the project root, to a project-owned doc of notes for the testing auditor: how the suites are laid out and the conventions they follow. It must exist in the checkout; a path that leaves the project is refused.

redundancy.description: How many auditors look at each quality characteristic in a full round. More finds more and costs more. Defaults to 1.

extraContext.description: Free text about the project for the code reviewer, carried over from the database row it replaces.

nightly.description: What the code reviewer does for the project each night besides its sweep. Read only by a code reviewer that runs on the owner's machine: a project whose sweep is still dispatched by GitHub Actions may set it, and nothing there runs it.

checks.description: The project's nightly checks: commands too slow to run on every pull request, run once a night instead. They run after the project's sweep, in the order written, in a fresh checkout of the default branch at its head, after `reviewer.setup`, with `reviewer.env` and databases of their own for `reviewer.databases`, and without the code reviewer's own credentials. No agent runs. A check that fails does not stop the checks after it, and opens an issue in the project with the end of its output; the issue is closed when a later night's checks all pass. A project that lists none gets no checkout and no run.

name.description: A short name for the check, shown in the log and in the failure issue.

command.description: The shell command that runs the check, with `sh -c` from the project root. A non-zero exit is a failing check, and so is a check stopped for running longer than a project command may.

reviewer.extraContext: The billing module is generated; review its generator, not its output.
